title: Her Father's Daughter
description: Air Force Senior Airman Tycoria Johnson joins a team of the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA) on a quest to search for remains of servicemembers loss during the Vietnam War. In that same mission, Johnson finds herself continuing her father's legacy. (U.S. Navy video by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Claire Farin)
keywords: recovery mission, DPAA, Vietnam Mi-17 crash, MIA, POW

(soothing music)

^- When we found out that Senior Airman Johnson was coming,
^goosebumps.
^This was big, especially for me because I was here.
Very, very proud that she's able to come.
I can't think of anything more rewarding than that.
(slow music)
- I saw that I was slotted for Vietnam
and it was the month of my dad's anniversary
so I had a lot of mixed emotions.
^I was excited and then it kind of hit me, like,
^wow, I'm going to do the exact same thing that he did.
What I remember the most is my dad always being gone
and then coming back with stories.
I was actually nine when he passed,
but I was in Hawaii so my whole childhood
I just remember him being in DPAA.
- He was a big man but he was also
just a really, really nice man.
He had been on multiple missions before the accident
so I knew him as the team sergeant and he came through,
set up for his teams, et cetera.
Pulling equipment from the warehouses.
- They're telling me stories and they'll talk
about how awesome he was at his job.
It really touched me.
It was great to hear and then it pushed me
to make sure I tried my best when I was here.
Going through this mission, it just opened my eyes
a little bit more about what we do and what happened then
in history and the lives that we lost.
It kind of hit me that I'm here, I'm a part of this now
so I kind of want to continue on strong.
I felt like I was finishing his mission for him.
It really motivated me to try my best for him.
The mission as a whole, what we're doing, why we're here,
I think it's pretty cool and it makes it worth it.
I'm proud of myself.
I never would've imagined doing anything like this.
It's kind of amazing to know that people
are still remembering him, and not just him but everyone
that was a part of that crash so it's heartwarming
to know that other people care.
- It's still a raw nerve for all of us.
It was a hard time.
You know, after 17 years you think it's gets easier.
It doesn't.
He's missed along with the rest of them very much so.
I'm just happy that his daughter was able to come
and be a part of this and I know he's proud.
I know he's looking down and smiling.
